report_name: LOCAL CYCLING AND WALKING INFRASTRUCTURE PLAN TECHNICAL REPORT Workington
how_pct_was_used: The PCT was used to validate identified desire lines by comparing them against the 'Go Dutch' scenario outputs and to analyze commuter cycle flows to inform the network planning process.
other_tools_developed: A prioritisation framework was developed using 20 criteria across categories of Effectiveness, Policy, Economic, and Deliverability to score and rank infrastructure improvements.
specific_evidence_of_impact: Workington secured £23m from the Towns Fund in March 2021, which includes projects for improved pedestrian crossings, enhanced wayfinding, and new public realm improvements on Murray Road and Central Way. Additionally, accelerated funding has been used to improve the underpass and footway/cycle path on Central Way near the leisure centre.
pct_usage_quote: The link between Workington and Seaton, consisting of Calva Brow, Workington Road, Seaton Road and Main Road, appears to be the most popular route in all current and future scenarios in the Propensity to Cycle Tool (PCT) (see www.pct.bike for further information on the PCT). This route records less than 50 cyclists per day, reflecting the potential growth for cycling within the study area.
